newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: Mongolia's new president takes oath of office.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia's new president takes oath of office.

text.p: Mongolia's new President N. Bagabandi was sworn in on Friday and pledged to do his best to curb crime, end poverty and to work to cohabit with the government.

Bagabandi, 47, leader of the formerly communist opposition Mongolian People's Revolutionary Party (MPRP), swept to victory in presidential elections last May, defeating incumbent Punsalmaagiin Ochirbat who was backed by the government.

"I will work constructively...in cooperation with the parliament and the government within my legal authority, paying attention especially to economic and social matters," he said in his inauguration speech.
"Mongolia can't overcome its present problems through quarrelling or blaming the new society," he said. "We need to reunite our efforts and work to improve (people's) lives."
The new president, dressed in traditional Mongolian robes and boots, was sworn in before an audience of several hundred people in government house.
At the end of the ceremony he drank from a silver goblet containing mare's milk, a traditional Mongolian gesture marking the conclusion of an agreement.
Mongolia's president is largely a figurehead, but has the power to block legislation.

Diplomats say members of the reformist Democratic Union Coalition government have privately expressed concern over potential differences with the new president, especially over ambitious reforms for land privatisation.
The reformist coalition, which had backed Ochirbat for re-election, controls parliament, although it is one seat short of the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto.
Bagabandi praised Mongolia's progress on democracy and reform but said improvements in people's lives had lagged, citing inadequate social security, an industry in recession and increasing poverty.
"There has come a time to make changes so that the state treats citizens equally and society pays attention to the people," he said.
"I drew up my manifesto based on the saying 'the state for the citizens and society for the people' and as the president I will carry out all my actions in accordance with this saying," he said.
